title: Misanthropy
text: “Guh… haah… haah…”

Itsuki felt himself nearly swallowed by hatred welling up from the depths of his heart, but he couldn’t afford to lose his reason here, and so he held himself back by switching his bow away the moment he noticed Mole’s shallow breathing, I say. He destroyed the chains that had left Mole dangling in midair with an arrow, then caught them up in his arms.
“Itsuki… san… you… are…?”
“I’m sorry. I’m not Naofumi-san, the Shield Hero you all were waiting for… I’m the Bow Hero who’d been condemning him.”
Mole turned its eyes toward the noble’s corpse.
“It’s fine. This was my decision. Emia-san, just as you’d resolved yourself to… I wanted to save you.”

That meant betraying her wish to have sacrificed her life for someone else’s sake. And for that, he bore the sin of having killed a man. He had chosen to act not for justice, but for the person standing before him.

Even if someone told him he was wrong, even if the bow itself no longer recognized him as a hero, he would not regret this decision. If they wanted to call it evil, then let them call it evil all they liked.
He had thrown away justice. So now, he would no longer cling to means and methods. On this path, there was no need for scales to measure what was right.

Wrong methods, selfishness, arrogance—none of it mattered anymore. He could no longer allow their tyranny to continue. Even if someone appeared to punish him for it, he didn’t care. He had something he wanted to protect, even if it meant striking down whoever came to punish him for it. Itsuki swore that every time someone appeared to block this path, he would draw his bow against them.
“Emia-san, even if you deny me for this… I’ve already decided.”

He would mete out punishment to those he could not forgive, good and evil be damned. This wasn’t some mission given to him by someone else, nor a sense of righteousness. Even if this made him evil, even if only darkness awaited him down this road, it would be enough if the person he wanted to save was saved.
“F-fueeeh… th-there’s a loud noise coming from next door… wh-what happened?”
“Guh…”

Itsuki judged that he lacked the manpower to rescue Mole and escape from here, and so he headed toward the location of the voice belonging to someone he’d judged trustworthy during his time living here. He destroyed the locked door with an arrow and kicked it open.
“Fueeeeh!?”
Then, entering the room, he drew his bow taut and declared to Riska:

“Now that things have come to this, I’m ordering you to help me escape from here. You understand what happens if you refuse, right? If you make a sound, I’ll kill you… You’re a good person. I won’t treat you badly. So please, just obey quietly if you can.”
“Fueeeh!? Wh-what in the world is—”
While threatening Riska, Itsuki brought her to the room where he had killed the noble.
“Fu—”
“Do you understand now? I can already predict what would happen if I left you here. So I’m taking you with me by force.”

Well, there was also the possibility that Riska would end up being blamed as the culprit. Having realized the truth, Itsuki apparently had the presence of mind to consider even that. It also seemed to reflect the trust he’d built in Riska’s character through everything that had happened up to that point.
“Now then, Emia-san, let’s escape from here. I won’t let you refuse. No matter what happens, I’ll save you.”
“Itsuki-san…”

Leaping onto her shoulder, Itsuki threatened Riska into carrying Mole on her back, I say. After that, they swiftly and silently recovered their SP, then used a cloaking skill to quietly escape the mansion, and then the town, or so it seems.

“After that, things just sort of flowed—I had Rishia-san carry Emia-san on her back, and we fled to somewhere that seemed safe. After treating her wounds and waiting for her strength to recover, we made our way here. I told Rishia-san the whole situation, including that I’m the Bow Hero, and she helped me out whenever we needed to shop in towns and such.”
“Bwuh…”
“Well, along the way here I ended up slaughtering a few nobles and merchants who rubbed me the wrong way, so our group grew a bit.”
“It’s only been a little while since I last saw you, but… you’ve, uh, really been through quite an ordeal, haven’t you, Itsuki?”
Father was giving Itsuki a look of sympathy, I say. And as if to make a point of it, he showed off his severed tail through a gap in his robe, as if to say ‘see, this is real.’
“Isn’t that the same for you? You’re the Shield Hero, hunted by the entire nation.”
“W-well…”
“Man, that guy’s been through it too… half his tail’s gone.”
“Sometimes there are people who try to cut off the ears and tails of demi-humans and beastmen. Their excuse is something like… making them closer to human, was it…”
Crocodile Guy said this.
“How awful…”

Father sent a sympathetic gaze toward Itsuki’s tail, I say. Well, in Father’s case, no matter which loop it was, he always went out of his way to treat the wounds of slaves who’d been hurt like this. It started with Big Sister, and he’d shown considerable consideration for the villagers as well. Incidentally, in this loop, it was Rabbit Guy and Wolf who fit that bill.
“Anyway, that’s how I—foolishly used by this country to their convenience—ended up realizing the truth, exactly as that usaunny had intended.”
“I-I see…”
“Bwu bwu bwu…”

According to Yuki-chan’s translation of Riska’s account, what that noble had been doing was utterly monstrous, and apparently, upon investigating during their escape, they found that several demi-humans had already died. Itsuki seemed to keep telling Riska that what he was doing wasn’t justice, but Riska appeared to be drawn to him all the same, moved by the way he carried himself. Along the way, it seemed he’d treated her with careful, gentle consideration. Sometimes he tried to let her go, out of gratitude for her cooperation, but it seemed Riska kept following him regardless.
“Naofumi-san, there must be a reason you’re doing something like this too, right? I’m not doubting you anymore, so won’t you tell me? Why pretend to be a slave trader?”
“Well, the circumstances are a bit different from yours, Itsuki, but… yeah. It’s true it all started when I saved a girl who was being tortured as a slave.”
Father seemed to be recalling the moment he’d rescued Big Sister, I say.
“I knew it. This country must be full of countless things like that—more than you alone could ever hope to save, Naofumi-san.”
Itsuki seemed to understand deeply, I say. Incidentally, the Mole that Father had taken in was clinging to him now, practically advertising how attached it had become.
“Certainly, as far as I’m concerned, I feel like I’ve been through an extraordinary experience, but experiences like this are commonplace in this world. Still, I did gain quite a bit from it.”
“You don’t have to be so resigned about it, you know… well, I’m just glad we could reconcile, Itsuki.”
“Yeah… but somehow, I realized that I’ve come to hate this creature called ‘human.’”
“Hm?”
Itsuki turned toward Father and Ren with eyes that seemed to reflect a darkness even deeper than a curse.

“Thinking back on it, it started with those meritocratic people from my old world who judged me by my abilities, then the ones who exploited me for nothing but the title of ‘Hero,’ and then the ones who took the opportunity to hurl magic at Naofumi-san. Just remembering their faces makes this feeling swell up inside me. Ahh… this species truly makes me sick.”
I don’t believe he had turned into a Cursed weapon, but something about Itsuki’s demeanor was definitely off.

“Naofumi-san, you’re the Hero of the demi-humans and beastmen, aren’t you? I’ve come to feel tremendously envious of that. Yes, this world truly belongs to demi-humans and beastmen. Once I’ve destroyed this country, I want to become the guardian of a nation of demi-humans and beastmen.”
“H-hold on, Itsuki?”
Itsuki looked around, scanning his surroundings restlessly.
“But wait, where’s that damn rabbit… Naofumi-san, where’s that rabbit-eared fellow who kept picking fights with me?”
Rabbit Guy spun around in an instant, bolting like a startled hare, trying to flee the scene. But Itsuki spotted him immediately and pinned his shadow to the ground with an arrow.
“Gah! My body!”
Rabbit Guy instantly figured out why he couldn’t move and unleashed a spell of light to break free, but by then Itsuki had already caught up to him and mounted his back.
